structured_output.hypothesis: If all living things share chemical composition, cellular structure and laws of growth and reproduction, then a large set of genes encoding core molecular machinery (translation, replication, transcription) must have recognisable orthologs across the sampled bacterial and archaeal genomes, which are the most distant cellular lineages.
structured_output.pass_criterion: At least 50 COGs are present in at least 95% of the 2,296 genomes (2,103 bacterial and 193 archaeal) in COG2024. These include members of functional categories J (translation), K (transcription) and L (replication). The core COGs must reach at least 95% coverage in bacteria and in archaea separately.
structured_output.fail_criterion: Fewer than 10 COGs are present in at least 90% of genomes across both domains, or none of the universally shared COGs belongs to category J (translation, ribosomal structure).
structured_output.interpretation: Darwin's "chemical composition, germinal vesicles, cellular structure, laws of growth and reproduction" are mapped to shared molecular machinery for building and reproducing cells: orthologous genes for ribosomal proteins, DNA replication and transcription. This is a modern reinterpretation. The dataset covers only Bacteria and Archaea, so it cannot test plants and animals directly. It tests the claim at the deepest divide in cellular life. It does not test the poison-effect example. The claim is stated for all living things, so this plan covers only part of its scope. Eukaryote coverage would need a supplementary resource.

dataset.name: COG - NCBI (Database of Clusters of Orthologous Genes, COG2024)
dataset.why_it_fits: COG2024 covers 2,103 bacterial and 193 archaeal species with orthologous gene clusters and functional categories. Files are at https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pub/COG/COG2024/data/. The fields to use are the COG-to-genome membership tables and the COG functional category letters (J, K, L), which give the per-COG genome presence fraction.

input.prompt: Give the page title, what the database is, download/FTP options, and any DOI.

input.hypothesis: If all living things share chemical composition, cellular structure and laws of growth and reproduction, then a large set of genes encoding core molecular machinery (translation, replication, transcription, energetics) must have recognisable orthologs across the sampled bacterial and archaeal genomes, which are evolutionarily the most distant cellular lineages.
input.pass_criterion: At least 50 COGs (clusters of orthologous genes) are present in at least 95% of the 2,296 genomes (2,103 bacterial and 193 archaeal) in COG2024, and these include the functional categories J (translation) and L (replication) and K (transcription), with the shared-core COGs present in both domains (each domain at least 95% coverage separately).
input.fail_criterion: Fewer than 10 COGs are present in at least 90% of genomes across both domains, or the universally shared COGs contain no members of category J (translation, ribosomal structure), which would show no common molecular core.
input.interpretation: Darwin's "chemical composition, germinal vesicles, cellular structure, laws of growth and reproduction" are mapped to the shared molecular machinery for building cells and reproducing them: orthologous genes for ribosomal proteins, DNA replication, transcription and core metabolism. This is a modern reinterpretation. The dataset covers only Bacteria and Archaea, so it cannot test plants and animals directly. It tests the claim at the deepest divide in cellular life and does not test the poison-effect example. Eukaryote coverage would need a supplementary resource. This is a limit of the test and a scope narrowing that the plan states openly.
